Composition: 925 sterling silver is an alloy composed of 92.5% pure silver and 7.5% other metals, typically copper. Purpose of Alloy: Pure silver is too soft for practical use in jewelry, so it is alloyed with other metals to increase its strength and durability. Authenticity Mark: The "925" stamp is a common hallmark used to certify the authenticity and purity of sterling silver jewelry.

det.desc: This is what I learn about: Gaze at a Talavera pottery urn, vase or platter, the finest ceramics of Mexico, and behold the art of a Spanish colonial period rich with old world design and a colorful heritage. The rich Talavera pottery heritage was introduced to Mexico by Spanish guild artisans of the Colonial period. Commonly called "majolica" in Spain, Mexican Talavera draws its name from the 16th century Spanish pottery center, Talavera de la Reina. While the intricate polychrome and more typical blue and white designs show their Old World legacy, native floral and animal motifs claim these colorful ceramics as classically Mexican.

rows.t: Vintage Japanese Moriage Porcelain Vase  Samurai Scene – Showa Era c.1930

det.desc: This is a stunning vintage Japanese hand painted moriage-style vase, dating to the early Showa period (circa 1926–1940s). The vase is crafted from white porcelain and features vivid hand-painted detailing with traditional raised moriage enamel. The intricate scene depicts Japanese figures in ceremonial attire, likely samurai or nobles, framed by ornate scrollwork in rich reds, greens, blues, and golds. The scalloped rim, bold relief decoration, and the red-painted base over porcelain are characteristic of Japanese export porcelain from this era. The vase is approximately 6 “ tall and 5 “ wide, in excellent vintage condition, with no cracks or repairs. The only spot missing slip ( blue ) is on the ruffed rim ( see pic ). The interior shows signs of past use — likely from holding fresh flowers — including light staining or mineral deposits consistent with age. These do not affect display and could likely be cleaned further if desired. A beautiful collector’s piece or decorative accent for lovers of Asian antiques, Japanese art, or moriage ware.

det.desc: Title: A Man's Path Date: May 2026 Medium: color pencil Type: Limited edition art print Art Description: A Man's Path is 11'' x 14'' color pencil fanart illustration of Gyro Zeppeli, a character from Steel Ball Run by Hirohiko Araki, best known for Jojo's Bizarre Adventures. Through Araki's character design and storytelling of Gyro, masculinity and what it means to be a man is presented through self expression, authenticity, and forging your own path, "the shining path." Cowboys hold significance not only in cishetero culture but in queer culture as well. In this piece, I wanted to play with color theory techniques to create vivid colors that encapsulate the passion and drive to find one's own way in the world, regardless of the consequences. I used vibrant colors as a way of expressing queer joy and how cohesively it exists within and alongside masculinity, especially in an American Western context. On the personal side, I based his skin tone off my dad's, a Midwestern farmer -- tanned from the outdoors with a reddish hint of sunburn.

det.desc: Up for sale is an incredibly unique, highly collectible fine art printmaking set by Pacific Northwest artist believed to be Ed Magic (signed "EM"). This listing is not just for a single print, but a complete 3-piece progressive process set that perfectly demonstrates the complex mechanics of reduction block printing. Because reduction block printmaking (often called the "suicide method") requires the artist to progressively carve away and destroy the single printing block layer by layer, these early passes can never be recreated. The artist intentionally set aside these sheets mid-run to archive the evolution of the piece. What is Included in This Set: • The 1st Pass Proof: The very first ink impression pulled from the block, showing the base layer and earliest background colors. • The 5th Pass Proof: A highly developed mid-stage impression showing the compounding complexity, depth, and color alignment. • The Final Masterpiece Print: The completed, multi-layered reduction print—fully hand-signed by the artist and titled “Frogbound Red” Item Specifications: • Artist: Ed Magic (Signed "EM") • Origin: Washington State, USA (Pacific Northwest Regional Fine Art) • Medium: Multi-color Re
